FV-G Band Duties (Administrative Officer): Incumbent is responsible for providing advice and guidance on varying fiscal and administrative matters to management. Provides or secures the resources or services needed to run the organization.

The work involves direct assistance to the supervisor who has the primary responsibility for the direction of the organization established to accomplish the mission.

As the office Administration Professional, assists managers and staff in projecting staffing needs, including staffing levels and grades, and conducts work flow studies within the organization. Coordinates with HR to obtain guidance as it relates to organizational related functions including pay, leave, and benefits.

Reviews travel associated matters and the training program including initial and recurring. Responsible for managing the office logistics program including personal property, supplies and services, and acquisition activities, awards, OSHA, security, and vehicle management.

Identifies, analyzes, and recommends solutions to recurring problems and offers recommendations for improvements. Interprets guidelines and provides management with advice and counsel on the operation of assigned programs and interrelationships of such programs.

Most assignments are completed without direct supervision as established in the guidelines. Some discretion is given to select the most appropriate approach. FV-H Band Duties (Administrative Officer): Tracks and analyzes data to ensure compliance with policies and procedures.

Responsible for coordinating and performing multiple and varying assignments under the general direction of the manager. May work as a team member on various projects. Responsible for planning time and assisting others to plan and use assigned resources to complete tasks.

Responsible for coordinating and accomplishing administrative tasks in a wide range of administrative and analytical duties. Evaluates and monitors office expenditures and makes sound changes based on trends and analysis, merit and deficiency situations, and known or anticipated program changes.

Performs immediate and long-range planning and control for organizational services independently, anticipating program changes, etc. Coordinates with Human Resources for advice on advisory services as they relate to organizational functions including pay, leave, and benefits.

Reviews travel associated matters and manages the training program including initial and recurring. Responsible for managing the office logistics program including personal property, supplies and services, and acquisition activities, awards, OSHA, security, and vehicle management.

Procures office supplies and equipment and closely monitors expenditures and reviews purchase card statements for accuracy.
FV-G: To qualify for this position, you must demonstrate in your application that you possess at least one year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to FV-F (FG/GS 5/7/9).

Specialized experience is defined as experience organizing office administrative functions in support of daily operations and purchasing supplies and equipment adhering to regulatory and procedural requirements; experience using computer software applications to prepare spreadsheets, correspondence, presentations, graphs, etc.; and support management in tracking and managing various administrative and operations programs and projects.

FV-H: To qualify for this position, you must demonstrate in your application that you possess at least one year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to FV-G (FG/GS 10/11).

Specialized experience is defined as experience in applying management principles, methods and techniques to solve problems of the organization; experience with the general management of an organization; experience developing and securing fiscal and business resources and services needed to manage and run an organization.

OR; Education substitution for FV-G: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree OR a combination of education and experience may be qualifying for this position.

Education at the graduate level in an accredited college or university must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work. There is no education substitution at the FV-H level.

Foreign education must be evaluated by a private professional organization specializing in interpretation of foreign education credentials or an accredited US educational institution in terms of equivalency to a degree acquired at an American college or university.

A copy of the evaluation results must be included, otherwise your foreign education will not be considered. If you are qualifying based upon your education, you must submit your college transcripts. If selected, official college transcripts will be required. Qualifications must be met by the closing date of this announcement.

The duties and responsibilities for a GS-0301-14 Lead Administrative Specialist-14 generally include, but are not limited to, the following: Serve as advisor to assigned program areas in support of administrative services in the areas of personnel management, safety, space management, and/or other general administrative functions.

Manage, operate, and maintain documents/data into diverse automated systems to process or obligate payment for delivery/acquisition of services. Establish measurable performance metrics for administrative support functions and report those metrics to upper office management. Report to upper management deadlines and/or priorities set.

Serve as the security program manager providing responsibility for the continuity of operations program, the operational security (OPSEC) program, and is the occupant emergency coordinator.
To qualify for the position of Lead Administrative Specialist, at GS-0301-14, you must meet the qualification requirements listed below. There may also be a positive education requirement for some occupations, please see the Education section for details.

If there are licensing or certification requirements, please see the Required Documents section for details on how to verify you license or certificate.

For the GS-14: Specialized Experience: For the GS-14, you must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service which demonstrates providing advisory for administrative services to staff in areas such as personnel management, facility or space management.

No Substitution allowed at the GS-14 grade level. You MUST meet all qualification requirements, including time-in-grade, by 07/23/2026 of this announcement. Your resume must support your responses to the application questionnaire and the qualification requirements. Failure to do so may result in an ineligible rating.

See the Required Documents section for important notes about what must be included in your resume.

Analyze staffing levels, travel, materials, and related requirements to provide cost data and information for program planning and evaluation activities.
Evaluate budgetary and fiscal data for consistency with estimates, current program operations, and anticipated changes in mission, staffing, and funding.
Provide policy interpretation and guidance regarding the preparation, revision, monitoring, and evaluation of organizational budget estimates and FTE needs.
Advise OPPD management officials on human resources matters by coordinating organizational needs with human resources office requirements.
Initiate personnel actions and oversee recruitment, selection, promotion, awards, and training activities to ensure alignment with staffing plans and funding levels.
Advise OPPD management officials in structuring positions and writing performance plans.
Review completed position descriptions and work plans for format and uniformity before submission to the human resources office.
To qualify for this position, applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement. Specialized Experience: Specialized experience is experience directly related to the position to be filled. Specialized experience must be described for grade level advertised.

The specialized experience requirements for this position are: To qualify for the Administrative Officer GS-11 level, you must demonstrate in your application that you possess at least one year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-09 level in the that equipped you with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of this position.

Specialized experience must show evidence of performing administrative management functions in support of organizational operations, including budget, personnel, procurement, and office services.

Your resume must show you have performed all duties similar to these: Supporting human resources functions, such as initiating personnel actions; assisting with recruitment activities (including advising managers on hiring authorities, timelines, and documentation requirements), selection, promotion, reassignment, awards, and training processes; reviewing position descriptions or work plans for accuracy; or coordinating actions with servicing HR offices; developing HR related reports for managerial review.

Supporting new employee orientation by ensuring completion of required forms, verifying documentation, and coordinating with HR and the hiring manager. Providing routine guidance to employees on basic personnel procedures such as time and attendance, leave, training, or award submissions.

Compiling and analyzing administrative or program data, such as staffing levels, workload changes, travel, supplies, or other resource needs, and preparing summaries or reports used for planning or evaluation purposes.

Assisting with or performing budget-related duties, including compiling resource requirements, reviewing financial data for consistency with established estimates, and preparing portions of an organizational budget submission.

Applying administrative policies, procedures, or regulatory requirements to resolve routine issues related to personnel, budgeting, procurement, or office operations.

Assisting with procurement and contract-related tasks, including preparing requisitions or purchase requests, monitoring purchases for compliance, or providing guidance on basic contracting or property management procedures.

Providing administrative support services, such as records management, property management, travel processing, mail and file services, equipment maintenance, or similar operational activities.

Communicating with internal and external stakeholders, such as program staff, agency representatives, contractors, or partner organizations, in order to exchange information, coordinate administrative actions, or provide guidance on procedural requirements.

To qualify for the Administrative Officer GS-12 level, in addition to the above, you must demonstrate in your application that you possess at least one year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-11 level in the that equipped you with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of this position.

Specialized experience must reflect independent application of advanced administrative management practices across budget, human resources, procurement, and organizational support functions within a complex program environment.

Your resume must show you have performed all duties similar to these: Providing authoritative guidance on staffing needs, classification issues, drafting and updating position descriptions, documenting duties, and personnel policy interpretation.

Acting as a liaison with HR to advise management officials on human resources matters and coordinating organizational needs with servicing HR offices. Conducting analyses of administrative support structures, recommending improvements to position management and workflow processes.

Identifying and resolving complex multifaceted administrative problems impacting financial management, personnel utilization, logistics, and office operations, often under conditions requiring independent judgment, competing priorities, and limited guidance.

Interpreting and applying procurement and contract regulations, directing staff in preparing requisitions and purchase orders, and ensuring adherence to Federal and Agency acquisition policies.

Advising management officials and employees on contract management responsibilities, procurement options, and compliance obligations that impact personnel or administrative operations.

Interpreting HR policies and regulatory requirements to address sensitive or complex staffing issues; coordinating with HR specialists, program managers, and other partners to address complex personnel operational needs or policy related questions.

Providing tactful and effective communication with internal and external partners, including program managers, employees, contractors, and other agencies, to implement recommendations or secure cooperation on sensitive issues.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Difference-at-Grade Justification Notes: The Administrative Officer position is established as a career-ladder GS-09/11/12 role, with the GS-12 representing the Full Performance Level (FPL).

The differences between the GS-11 and GS-12 levels reflect increased independence, complexity, judgment, and program impact, all of which are documented in the position description. The GS-12 Administrative Officer functions as the fully independent, authoritative administrative expert for OPPD.

This level requires: -Greater judgment and initiative -Broad programmatic impact -Independent interpretation of guidelines -Higher complexity of assignments -Strategic advising of OPPD leadership -Oversight of integrated administrative systems In contrast, the GS-11 serves in a developmental capacity, performing portions of these responsibilities but lacking the full independence, scope of influence, and complexity required at the GS-12 level.

These distinctions align with the Factor Level descriptions and Statements of Difference outlined in the PD.

Serves as the Chief of the Administrative Division and administrative advisor to the U.S. Attorney for planning and managing the United States Attorney's Office resources.

Typical duties include but are not limited to: Planning and managing a comprehensive administrative support program that includes the spectrum of administrative support services, e.g., budget, administration, personnel, space management, purchasing, information technology management, internal controls, mail, records, acquisitions, communication services and supplies.

Supervising a subordinate staff of administrative, technical and clerical personnel. Setting goals and priorities. Preparing schedules for completion of work. Analyzing management issues for the district, developing short- and long-range plans to ensure office operations are conducted efficiently and effectively and meet mission requirements.

As a Designated Operating Plan district, exercising significant autonomy for short- and long-range budget administration. On behalf of the U.S. Attorney, serves as the primary financial manager for the district; responsible for budget formulation, presentation to EOUSA and execution.

Developing and managing a comprehensive district-level personnel program exercising final authority for personnel planning and management activities to meet the short- and long-range needs of the office.

Planning and providing for all management services and office support functions in the district which include printing, publications, automation, selection of furniture and equipment, property management and supplies.

Overseeing the purchasing program to ensure purchases are within delegated authority and comply with all associated policies, procedures, and guidelines. Managing the information technology program for the district ensuring employees have hardware and software needs to meet mission requirements.

Projecting and analyzing space needs based on proposed initiatives, staff changes and technology improvements. Designing office layouts, schedules alterations and repairs, overseeing building renovation and directing the relocation of personnel to new space.
GS-15: To be eligible at the GS-15 level, you must have at least ONE year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 level in Federal Service.

Specialized experience includes experience performing the following: 1) managing the distribution of staff workload to meet the mission of an organization; 2) providing advisory and technical advice to senior management officials on administrative program areas; 3) developing and maintaining a system of internal controls and accountability; and 4) supervising or managing an office or organization overseeing three or more of the following administrative program areas: (a) Budget; (b) Human Resources (HR); (c) Information Technology (IT); (d) Acquisitions and/or Contracting; or e) Property/Space Management.

Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP)- The CTAP provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies.

If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy.

To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and receive a score of 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.

Additional information about CTAP eligibility is at http://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/employee-guide-to-career-transition/.

THIS IS AN AIR RESERVE TECHNICIAN OFFICER POSITION. Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing; computer skills to generate data in spreadsheets and reports. 5. Knowledge of safety, security, and EEO regulations, practices, and procedures. 6. Ability to analyze current or projected AE operations programs, and AE program management functions, principles, and techniques. 7.

Business acumen to ensure organizational mission accomplishment; must demonstrate fiscal responsibility and accountability for allocated squadron resources. 8. Ability to resolve complex issues, maintain good working relations. 9.

Ability to manage/coordinate health services programs to include: logistics, facilities, finance, operations/support, human resources, patient administration, AE, communications/information systems and operational reporting systems. 10.

Comprehensive knowledge of Air Force, DoD, and civilian sector operational health care systems to include, ancillary/support services, managed and contract care, medical operations and in-route medical support, and adjunct health care systems. 11.

Ability to plan, organize, and direct an AE system infrastructure and medical/aeromedical operations. 12. Knowledge of medical readiness planning and training requirements and administrative staff functions. 13. Ability to plan, organize, and assign work to subordinate employees.

PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week.

The duties and responsibilities for a Administrative Specialist, GS-0341-9/11 generally include, but are not limited to, the following: Coordinating administrative programs in areas such as human resources, budget and finance, procurement, travel, records, facilities, training, security, telecommunications, and information resources.

Evaluating administrative operations and supporting services to identify opportunities for improving organizational efficiency and effectiveness. Monitoring administrative actions and projecting requirements to ensure compliance with program guidance and established deadlines.

Analyzing administrative data and operational trends to develop recommendations for improving processes and use of resources. Providing technical guidance on administrative regulations, policies, procedures, and program requirements. Preparing management reports and status information to support decisions and follow-up on administrative actions.

Coordinating with internal offices, other government organizations, and vendors to address administrative requirements and operational issues.
In order to qualify for the Administrative Specialist position, you must meet the following minimum qualifications: FOR THE GS-09 LEVEL: Specialized Experience: Applicants must have at least one year (52 weeks, full-time) of specialized work experience equivalent to the GS-07 level in the Federal service (or comparable experience outside the Federal service), performing 3 or more of the following duties: Reviewing administrative program information to identify procedural issues affecting office operations; Tracking administrative requests or project actions through established processes to support timely completion; Monitoring procurement or property activities for compliance with established administrative procedures; and Coordinating administrative support with internal staff or external service providers to address routine operational needs.

(Your resume must CLEARLY demonstrate this experience) -OR- Education: Applicants must have a master's OR equivalent graduate degree, OR two (2) full academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a master's or equivalent graduate degree, or LL.B. or J.D. in a directly related field, that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position.

NOTE: Applicants must submit a copy of their transcripts for verification. -OR- Combination of Education and Experience: Applicants must possess a combination of the above described education and specialized experience such that they total 100% of the stated minimum qualifications for the GS-09 level.

Only graduate education beyond one (1) year, i.e., 18 semester hours, may be combined with experience under this provision. NOTE: Applicants must submit a copy of their transcripts for verification.

FOR THE GS-11 LEVEL: Specialized Experience: Applicants must have at least one year (52 weeks, full-time) of specialized work experience equivalent to the GS-09 level in the Federal service (or comparable experience outside the Federal service), performing 3 or more of the following duties: Coordinating a designated administrative program to ensure actions meet established program requirements; Analyzing administrative operations to identify trends and recommend improvements in organizational efficiency; Preparing administrative status reports to identify issues requiring management attention; and Applying administrative regulations and procedures to resolve program issues with limited supervisory guidance.

(Your resume must CLEARLY demonstrate this experience) -OR- Education: Applicants must have a Ph.D.

OR equivalent doctoral degree, OR three (3) full academic years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree, or LL.M. in a directly related field, that demonstrates the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work of the position.

NOTE: Applicants must submit a copy of their transcripts for verification. -OR- Combination of Education and Experience: Applicants must possess a combination of the above described education and specialized experience such that they total 100% of the stated minimum qualifications for the GS-11 level.

Typical duties include, but are not limited to Advises the Veteran Readiness and Employment Officer on practical and technical aspects of office administration to include budgeting, supply management, information resource and files management, and perform staff support work in each of these areas.

Reviews work measurement functions of the operations of the Division and ensures that reporting requirements and procedures are met.

Actively assists the Vocational Readiness and Employment Officer in budgeting and controlling General Operating Expense (GOE) funds for the Division; prepares quarterly estimates of funds for each Division account; maintains Fund Control Point balances, records quarterly allotments, expenditures, and adjustments using Excel spreadsheets.

Receives output from the Financial Management System (FMS) and verifies local Control Point balances. Immediately clarifies variances with accounting Section personnel and the station Budget Analyst.

Continuously analyzes accounts to determine shortages or surplus, adjusting accordingly and immediately advises the Budget Officer of surpluses or shortages as they occur.

Prepares recurring and special summary reports on specific areas as requested by the Vocational Readiness and Employment Officer, and research inquiries from veterans and training institutions, contractors, service organizations and other interested parties.

Gathers information and statistical data from all operating elements and prepare and maintain various technical records and reports required by the Division. Reviews such data for completeness and accuracy and for the purpose of identifying specific trends and coordinates all activities concerning statistical and narrative reports.

This includes analyzing and/or verifying data submitted for Systematic Analysis of Operations (SAO) reports, and internal control reports. Responsible for monitoring AskVA (AVA) and future Veteran inquiry systems. Monitors Review of Quality data to include coordinating monthly reviews, obtaining files for review and completing appropriate paperwork.

Maintains the Readiness and Employment Division library, e.g., VA regulations, manuals, circulars, bulletins and other publications, and posts changes as needed. Distributes publications to appropriate employees and assists with administrative and clerical issues.

Responsible for receiving and properly distributing incoming mail, monitor all controlled correspondence, and maintain suspense records and diaries to ensure timely responses and/or actions are taken in accordance with office directives.

Receives and places telephone calls to a wide range of program participants and VA personnel in other divisions and offices. Provides specific information on routine matters falling within established procedures and redirects calls to the appropriate staff member based on knowledge of the program areas or operations.

Attends and participates with VR&E Division staff meetings and prepare and distribute approved minutes. Ensures that employee information is properly distributed, and that information posted to the division bulletin board is current.

Das Kommissariat Ermittlungen der Stadtpolizei Zürich stellt die kriminalpolizeiliche Grundversorgung bei Vergehen und Verbrechen im gesamten Stadtgebiet rund um die Uhr sicher. Nebst eigenen Ermittlungsaufträgen bearbeitet der dazugehörige Ermittlungsdienst auch Aufträge der Untersuchungsbehörden sowie von der Uniformpolizei übergebene Haftfälle.
Die Fälle werden von der ersten Abklärung bis zum Abschluss des Verfahrens bearbeitet, sofern keine spezialisierte Gruppe dafür zuständig ist. Sie begleiten das Geschehen von der Tatortarbeit über die Ermittlungen, Einvernahmen, Zwangsmassnahmen bis zur abschliessenden Rapportierung - nah am Fall, nah an der Praxis.
## Aufgaben ##
* Ausrücken an Tatorte zwecks Tatbestandsaufnahme und Koordination vor Ort bei relevanten kriminalpolizeilichen Ereignissen
* Sicherstellung der kriminalpolizeilichen Strafverfolgung bei Vergehen und Verbrechen sowie Treffen von Massnahmen zur Prävention derselben
* Durchführung von anspruchsvollen Ermittlungsverfahren, auch in Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Fachgruppen, den Untersuchungsbehörden sowie weiteren spezialisierten Diensten
* Teilnahme an Extradiensten und aktives Mitgestalten von eigenen Aktionen
* Leisten von kriminalpolizeilichen Nacht-, Wochenend- und Pikettdiensten (ca. 12 Nachtdienste pro Jahr)
## Profil ##
* Abgeschlossene Polizeiausbildung (Fachausweis Polizist\*in) und mehrjährige kriminalpolizeiliche Erfahrung oder Interesse, sich diesbezüglich zu entwickeln
* Fundierte polizeiliche Fachkenntnisse, Kenntnisse der relevanten Nebengesetzgebungen sowie ein strukturiertes Vorgehen bei komplexen Tatbestandsaufnahmen
* Schreibgewandtheit mit soliden Kenntnissen im Bereich der Rapportierung
* Interesse an umfassenden kriminalpolizeilichen Ermittlungen inkl. Tatortarbeit und delegierten Einvernahmen sowie hohe Motivation und Freude an eigenverantwortlicher und exakter Arbeitsweise
* Teamfähigkeit und Aufgeschlossenheit sowie ein professionelles Auftreten in der Zusammenarbeit mit unterschiedlichen Anspruchsgruppen
## Wir bieten ##
Eine herausfordernde, vielseitige und breitgefächerte Tätigkeit im kriminalpolizeilichen Bereich mit Anzeige- und Ausrückdienst, der Tatortarbeit sowie der vertieften Ermittlungstätigkeit. Sie werden sorgfältig und umfassend in Ihre tägliche Arbeit eingeführt.

Auf Sie warten adäquate und angepasste Aus- und Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten im kriminalpolizeilichen Bereich und die Arbeit im urbanen Umfeld mit einem modernen Arbeitsplatz in Zürich-West.

Attraktive Anstellungsbedingungen wie z.B. Übernahme von 60% der PK-Sparbeiträge, Mobilitätsbeitrag von bis zu CHF 600.00 pro Jahr und monatlich bis zu CHF 100.00 Verpflegungsentschädigung runden unser Angebot ab.

To be well-qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and receive a score of 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide proof of eligibility to receive selection priority.
